evidence_priority: recorded project decision or approved exception
repeated acceptable WIP corpus pattern in equivalent contexts
Persian-language consultant or Area Linguist judgement
finding_requirement: A project-grammar finding must cite one or more rule IDs. A general meaning finding must identify its non-grammar category explicitly.
finding_requirements: Cite the exact WIP form and reference.
Cite one or more FA-GR rule IDs for a grammar finding.
Distinguish grammar, orthography, style, and meaning risk.
Route unconfirmed rules and naturalness judgements to the assigned human reviewer.

governance.authority: Project-approved Persian grammar guidance, corpus evidence, and recorded consultant decisions

restrictions: Do not infer a project rule from one occurrence.
Do not treat the contemporary source grammar or word order as the Persian model.
Do not transfer Greek or Hebrew morphology directly into Persian grammar.
Do not normalise characters, ZWNJ, digits, or punctuation without project authority.

rules.caution: Do not replace characters automatically when the project has an established orthographic policy.
rules.review: Check Arabic/Persian character variants, combining marks, joining behaviour, and project-approved Unicode forms.

rules.caution: ZWNJ conventions vary by project and publication system; report evidence rather than normalising silently.
rules.review: Check word spacing, half-space or ZWNJ use, affixes, compounds, and joining around punctuation.

rules.caution: Do not infer an ezāfe error solely from the written absence of an optional visible marker.
rules.review: Check ezāfe relationships, adjective order, possessive relationships, apposition, and noun-phrase attachment.

rules.caution: Clitic placement interacts with register, emphasis, and written style; confirm the intended constituent.
rules.review: Check attachment and referents of object, possessive, copular, and connective clitics.

rules.caution: Formal and colloquial patterns differ; use the project register rather than a universal prescriptive rule.
rules.review: Check subject–verb agreement, animacy-sensitive plural agreement, person, number, and copular forms.

rules.caution: Do not map Greek, Hebrew, or English verbal forms mechanically to one Persian construction.
rules.review: Check tense, aspect, mood, evidential force, modality, and auxiliary combinations against the intended event structure.

rules.caution: Lexical choice and naturalness require Persian corpus and project evidence.
rules.review: Check light-verb constructions, compound predicates, valency, and selection of copular or verbal complements.

rules.caution: Persian permits subject omission; do not add names or pronouns merely to mirror a reference text.
rules.review: Check overt and omitted pronouns, antecedents, reflexives, demonstratives, honorific forms, and participant shifts.

rules.caution: Differences from English word order are not findings unless they affect meaning, clarity, or project style.
rules.review: Check topic–comment organisation, focus, scrambling, modifier placement, and ambiguity caused by constituent order.

rules.caution: Restructuring is acceptable when logical relationships and discourse prominence remain clear.
rules.review: Check relative clauses, complement clauses, conditionals, temporal clauses, and the scope of subordinators.

rules.caution: A particle difference alone does not establish a meaning error.
rules.review: Check negative scope, negative concord, interrogatives, imperatives, prohibitions, and indirect commands.

rules.caution: Persian may leave some relations implicit; assess whether the intended relation remains recoverable.
rules.review: Check causal, inferential, adversative, concessive, sequential, and explanatory relationships across clauses.

rules.caution: Apply the project’s publication conventions and do not import English punctuation mechanically.
rules.review: Check Persian punctuation, quotation marks, dialogue layout, terminal punctuation, and spacing around signs.

rules.caution: Final naturalness and community acceptability require qualified Persian speakers.
rules.review: Check contemporary Persian naturalness, audience register, idiom, and possible calques from the contemporary source.

rules.caution: Do not restructure a valid Persian sentence solely to mirror the contemporary source; require evidence of meaning, clarity, or project-policy impact.
rules.review: Check sentence division, clause attachment, parenthetical structure, coordination, and subordination where punctuation or connective choice permits competing parses.

usage.baseline_qa: Identify bounded evidence, corpus patterns, and review questions in the authorised scope.
usage.focused_check: Investigate one explicit Persian grammar or orthography concern.
usage.initialization: Validate language identity, schema, and approval status; do not perform verse-level grammar review.
usage.original_language_review: Clarify source meaning only when materially relevant; do not prescribe Persian form directly.
